text:
Anya K.: Heads-up: onboarding Pallas' LoRA finetune merge into our int4 runtime showed weird embedding collapse on a subset of their docs. quick context: merged LoRA → base-7B → quantized int4 profile, ran our eval pack (small, ~200 queries). Some examples have embeddings near-zero and duplicate vectors across different prompts.
Luke M.: ouch. did you run the tokenizer-remap step? sometimes new special tokens break the quant quantization pipeline.
Anya K.: yeah, ran tokenizer-remap and the usual qep. snippet I used: 
```bash
redwood eval run --model pallas-lora-merged:20260318 --quant int4-fast --eval-pack pallas-quick-200.json --out pallas-int4-smoke.json
```
Samir: can you paste an example pair (input → embedding) where they collapse? curious if it's limited to short prompts or specific unicode.
Anya K.: sending two examples inline: 
- "Invoice #4321 total": embedding vec mostly -0.0001 across dims
- "Can you summarize the attached policy?": nearly identical vector to the invoice example (cos sim ~0.997)
Cara: hmm that smells like token id collision or KV cache reuse when batch padding is mis-specified. Did you run with batching=1 to rule out batch-level noise?
Anya K.: I ran with batch size 8 (default). I can repro with batch 1, still shows duplicate vectors but lower frequency.
Luke M.: could be the LoRA merge process accidentally zeroed some projection rows for low-rank adapters under int4 quantization. Any merge logs?
Anya K.: merge logs attached in eval artifact (link: https://artifacts.redwood/pallas/1767012345/merge.log) — shows no obvious errors but weight-norm stats changed a lot on the last linear before pool.
Samir: try two quick things: 1) run the same merge but keep float32 weights (no quant) and run eval pack — if collapse disappears, it's quant artifact. 2) run quantize-only (no merge) on base-7B and eval — if collapse appears then base quant profile is the issue.
Anya K.: good plan. starting (1) now. ETA ~10m.
deploy-bot: model.pallas-lora-merged:20260318 pushed to staging at 2026-03-18T14:02:10Z :rocket:
infra-bot: infra: noticed a small change in kernel selection around 14:00 due to runtime optimizer roll (selector v2.3.1). rolling back to v2.3.0 for the staging pool is possible if needed.
Cara: also check embedding-normalization code path — our int4 runtime has a fast path that bypasses fp32 norm in some branches. if that's enabled it could saturate outputs.
Anya K.: results for (1) float32 merged run: no embedding collapse, vectors look distinct, cos sims <0.4 for those pairs. so it's quant-related.
Luke M.: ok that narrows it. next: try quantize-only on base-7B to confirm. if base quant shows problem, we might need a new calibration set or a tweak to per-channel scale.
Samir: if quant-only is fine, then try merging LoRA into an already-quantized base (merge-in-quant workflow) vs quant-after-merge — different numeric paths can diverge. run both and compare.
Anya K.: queued both workflows: 
- workflow A: base-7B (fp32) + merge LoRA → quant int4 (quant-after-merge)
- workflow B: base-7B quant int4 → merge LoRA into quant (merge-into-quant)
running A and B now on a small subset (20 prompts).
Cara: capture raw logits and pre-norm vectors if you can — that'll tell whether collapse happens pre- or post-normalization. also add a deterministic seed.
Anya K.: noted. attaching pre-norm dumps to artifacts when done.
Luke M.: if it reproduces, we'll try a quick hack: adjust quant bias correction on last-linear per-channel by +1e-3 and re-run eval pack (cheap and often fixes micro-collapses).
Anya K.: thanks all, will post results in ~20m. :thumbsup:
